correctness.rationale: The matching overlap graph decomposes the Hamiltonian into disjoint physical supports. Every two-string component is handled by local diagonalization for zero mismatch, a positive one-qubit conditional block for one mismatch, an exact commuting Gibbs Pauli expansion plus a negative one-qubit partial-transpose eigenvalue for even mismatch >=2, and an exact anticommuting Gibbs expansion plus a sharp two-site product expectation witness for odd mismatch >=3. Both necessity and sufficiency cover equality and arbitrary real coefficients. The three-qubit example is invariant under every partial transpose yet violates the full-separability witness above its explicitly solved threshold.

originality.rationale: The existing degree-one source-specific result establishes a single sharp worst-case threshold, not a complete classification of individual Hamiltonians at all temperatures. The new theorem classifies all components according to their local Pauli mismatch count and handles the single-incompatible-site regime, the commuting NPT transition, and the anticommuting PPT-but-not-fully-separable transition. The primary 2026 paper treats degree>=2 uniform thresholds; two-qubit thermal-entanglement and Pauli-witness literature do not subsume the exact many-qubit matching-graph result.
residual_risks: Pauli-feature entanglement witnesses for particular three-qubit families are known; an exact general two-string thermal classification might exist in differently indexed stabilizer-diagonal literature.
The classification is for full separability; the PPT odd-string example is not claimed to be entangled across a particular bipartition.
Pauli decomposition matters: the theorem assumes the specified overlap graph is a matching, not an optimization over all decompositions of the same Hamiltonian.

value.rationale: The anchor and earlier degree-one result identify a sharp worst-case thermal boundary but do not say when a particular matching-overlap Hamiltonian remains fully separable beyond it. The present theorem supplies a complete decision rule for every such Hamiltonian, introduces the local-incompatibility parity as the precise structural invariant, distinguishes finite versus absent entanglement transitions, and isolates a three-qubit Gibbs family that is PPT across every cut despite crossing a full-separability transition. This is a mathematically motivated exact classification relevant to Gibbs-state preparation and limitations of PPT diagnostics, not a routine parameter increment.
